riskFactors.title: 2026 Lease Expiry Concentration
riskFactors.description: ~40.5% of Mid Valley NLA expiring in 2026 creates a concentrated renewal event, but historical evidence supports this as a managed cyclical feature of IGB's active short-lease strategy (~3-year retail leases) rather than a novel structural risk. A 54.8% TGM NLA expiry concentration in FY2013 was navigated with no occupancy deterioration. Rental reversions have been positive (mid-single-digit) in recent cycles, and management has applied proactive forward-renewal strategy consistently since at least 2012.

quantitativeBacking.context: Elevated expiry concentration — managed cyclical event

mitigatingFactors.factor: Near-perfect occupancy (99.8% MVM) sustained through multiple prior expiry cycles
Historical precedent: 54.8% TGM NLA expiry in FY2013 navigated with no occupancy loss
Positive rental reversions confirmed in FY2024; mid-single-digit (4–6%) guidance
Proactive forward-renewal strategy documented in every AR since 2012
Deliberate short-lease structure (~3 years) to capture market-rate resets — industry standard
Diversified tenant base (top tenant AEON ~8% GRI); no single-tenant dependency

aggravatingFactors.factor: 40.5% concentration in a single year warrants monitoring
Specific annual renewal rate (% leases renewed) not publicly disclosed

monitoringTriggers: Rental reversion direction on completed renewals

riskFactors.title: IGB Berhad Sponsor Support
riskFactors.description: Long-standing sponsor relationship with demonstrated support through Southkey acquisition at favorable terms.

mitigatingFactors.factor: IGB Group 50+ year Malaysian property track record
